[[Category:Transformer]]
'''Self-attention''' is the process through which a [[Transformer]] enriches its [[token embedding (machine learning)|token embedding vectors]] with contextual information derived from other tokens in the same token sequence.<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref>

== Single-head attention ==

Let $\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}$ be the '''vector embedding matrix''' of [[token (machine learning)|token sequence]] $X$, in which row $t$ is the embedding vector for the token at position $t$.

$$
\mathbf{Q}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_Q,
\qquad
\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_K,
\qquad
\mathbf{V}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_V.
$$

where $\mathbf{W}_Q,\mathbf{W}_K,\mathbf{W}_V\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d_k}$ are '''weight matrices''' learnt during training (e.g., via [[backpropagation]]).

Then the standard attention score
$$
S_\text{attention}=\operatorname{Attention}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V})
=
\operatorname{row-wise\ softmax}\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)\mathbf{V},
$$

<blockquote>
The [[Softmax|softmax]] is taken row-wise so for each embedding vector $\vec x_t$ within $X$, $\sum_{i=1}^{d_k} (S_{\text{attention}})_{t,i} = 1$.

The scaling factor $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ keeps the scores from growing with the dimension.

Both are [[normalisation function]]s applied for numerical stability.
</blockquote>

<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref>

== Complexity ==

The complexity of standard self-attention

* Time $\propto O(T^2 d)$
* Memory $\propto O(T^2)$

where $O$ is the [[o(x) and o(x)|big-O notation]].

{{Hidden proof}}
Since

$$
\mathbf{Q}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d},\,
\mathbf{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}
$$

so

$$
\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times T}.
$$

Computing one entry of $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}$ is a dot product of length $d$:

$$
(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top})_{ij}
= \sum_{r=1}^{d} Q_{ir}K_{jr}.
$$

There are $T \times T = T^2$ such entries, and each costs $O(d)$ work. Therefore:

$$
\text{Time} \propto O(T^2 \cdot d)
$$

time to form the score matrix.

After that, attention also computes

$$
\mathrm{softmax}(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top})\mathbf{V},
$$

where $\mathbf{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}$. The softmax touches the $T\times T$ score matrix, costing $O(T^2)$

Finally, multiplying the $T\times T$ attention matrix by $\mathbf{V}$ costs another $O(T^2 d)$. So the attention cost is 

$$
\text{Time} \propto O(T^2 d)+O(T^2)+O(T^2 d)=O(T^2 d)
$$

Memory is $O(T^2)$ as only the final $T\times T$ score/attention matrix need to be stored in standard attention without additional caching.
{{End hidden}}

Generating a sequence of tokens in [[large language model (LLM)#Inference|inference]] recomputes most of this work unless the keys and values computed and cached, such as via [[KV caching]].

<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref>
